probability.label: Confident · 98%

probability.basis: The named son Caleb matches the established eldest Currituck child account and his six co-listed siblings, not just a repeated Caleb name. William Glasgow’s Currituck will, dated 14 October 1805 and recorded 22 January 1806, names wife Sarah, sons Caleb, Isaac, Samuel and John C., and daughters Ruth, Love Bright and Sophia. Its land divisions and household bequests identify one specific family. The named wife and all seven child names strongly identify the maintained William-357 family, with John C. compatible with John Cooper and Love now recorded under Bright; this conjunction outweighs the unsourced August death claim. The published transcription is by Judy Merrell Brickhouse, citing Currituck County Will Book 2, pp.279–280. The manuscript was not inspected. The will also transfers an enslaved boy; that clause does not add a biological family relationship.
